column1: # Accepted rises in tools/check_instructions.py, one per line and tab-separated:
# A line says why a rise was accepted when it was. The code it names may be gone since: the
# chunked event feed of AY-096 was removed by AY-117, and the typed read of `tiny` fell again.

column4: D82: before its first line, the writer looks through the value for tags that need a %TAG directive, about 75 instructions a document
D82: the look for tags that need a %TAG directive costs about 60 instructions a collection, and this input is 64 nested collections around one scalar
AY-096: the chunked event feed adds a branch per event to keep large typed documents below their peak target

AY-104: a typed read builds its value from events it takes from the parser one by one, and keeps no tree of the document; that costs about 160 instructions an item here, and an untyped decode of short scalars peaks 15% to 32% lower
AY-104: as for the short sequence, about 400 instructions an entry, part of them for a map that is no longer told its size
AY-104: as for the short sequence; each alias is still read from the anchored tree
pre-1.0 hardening PR: emitter.rs is untouched (Ir +0.00%); binary code layout shift from merge/frontmatter/Spanned hardening adds +5.25% simulated Callgrind EstCycles
pre-1.0 hardening PR: emitter.rs is untouched (Ir +0.09%); binary code layout shift from merge/frontmatter/Spanned hardening adds +5.61% simulated Callgrind EstCycles
AY-180: emit_flow_mapping disassembly is byte-identical (0 Ir delta); binary address shift causes Callgrind branch-predictor aliasing (+5.26% simulated EstCycles, +0.73% Ir)

AY-181: unifying <= 4 KiB typed decoding onto the streaming reader (D107) keeps Ir near-flat (+0.07%) while adding simulated cache/branch misses (+5.26% EstCycles) on unhinted 9-key Value decoding in exchange for -49.7% peak heap and -28.3% allocations
